`make verify` run 1 failed on one test, and it was a real bug in this change, not a flake.

`tests/unit/test_config_llm_known_keys.py::test_llm_known_keys_match_config_readers` AST-walks
the `[llm]` readers and asserts exact equality with `_LLM_KNOWN_KEYS` in
`src/rebar/_config_sections.py:216`. That tuple is a deliberate duplicate of the readers — the
core config parser must not import `rebar.llm`, because that is the optional `[agents]` extra —
so the test is what keeps the two in step.

My two new readers were not in it. The user-visible consequence: setting `[llm] embedding_model`
or `[llm] similar_digest_model` in `rebar.toml` would have warned "unknown key", and under
`REBAR_CONFIG_UNKNOWN_KEYS=error` it would have failed outright. The env vars worked, the
config file did not.

Fixed by adding both names to `_LLM_KNOWN_KEYS`, and documented both in the `[tool.rebar.llm]`
block in `docs/config.md` alongside their peers, which the first pass also missed.

This is the exact class `make lint` and `make typecheck` cannot see — both were green before the
run. Re-verified: `make lint` exit 0, the 1,067-test config/surface/env-registry selection
passes, the 18 docs-drift tests pass. Commit amended to `6f67b53d071` (Change-Id unchanged),
now 10 files. Full `make verify` re-running before push.
